figures.caption: Fig. 1. Schematic diagram illustrating the advantages of high-entropy sulﬁdes in ASSLSB. (a) The conﬁguration of a traditional ASSLSB, in which the electron and ion are respectively conducted by carbon and SE. During cycling, the sulfur particles isolated from carbon or SE cannot undergo the redox reaction and are rendered electrochemically inactive. (b) The conﬁguration of a HES-cooperated ASSLSB, in which the electron and ion conducting network is formed by high-entropy sulﬁdes. The sulfur particles around high-entropy sulﬁdes can be revitalized and actively participate in electrochemical reactions.
